mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows over the next 20 trading days, thereby lowering S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% in the month before decision
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar high-rate regimes (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: No significant correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE changes and SPX 60-day forward returns (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% suggests accelerating demand growth, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite sustained demand growth (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a sharp drop in the consumer confidence index (not in the catalog, so instead use HOUST) suggests contracting supply chains and weak demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 2% while HOUST falls by > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when both proxies move in the predicted direction.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%, it indicates a shift toward rate normalization, which elevates discount rates and dampens equity valuation multiples, producing negative 20-day forward returns for the S&P 500.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or flat during such FEDFUNDS crosses (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for two consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in labor force participation (not in catalog - use PAYEMS instead), implies a tight labor market that raises wage growth expectations and supports positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% for two consecutive months and PAYEMS increases month-over-month
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return in the 60-day window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a post-recession expansion phase (as signaled by a 3-month moving average of GDPC1 above 1.5% growth and UNRATE < 6%) is associated with higher expected corporate earnings and positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly higher than during comparable pre-expansion regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a period of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 3% for three consecutive months), the S&P 500 5-day forward return tends to be positive as lower borrowing costs ease financing constraints for growth stocks.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during such periods.
